title: Registering a Content Element

hints.text: A content element is a record type of tt_content, registered in Configuration/TCA/Overrides/tt_content.php with ExtensionManagementUtility::addRecordType(): the item — label, description, value, icon, group — then the showitem list for the type, then per-type overrides such as columnsOverrides, and optionally a position. The showitem list is the point: a type that does not bring one is a type whose backend form is somebody else's.

The predecessor is addPlugin() plus addToAllTCAtypes(), which registers the item and then patches the field list of every type. It is what an older extension looks like; a new record type is better added in one call.

addPlugin() is what is left for a plugin with a FlexForm, and it takes two arguments here — the item array and the FlexForm. The $field and $extensionKey arguments are gone, so the example that passes 'CType' and the extension key is from the branch before this one and is a TypeError on this one. It also seeds the new type's field list from the header type when the type declares none, so a plugin registered that way silently shows the header element's fields until a showitem replaces them.
A plugin is a CType like any other. The list_type detour, where one CType held every plugin and a second field chose between them, is gone, so what used to be a list_type value is a CType value now.

hints: ExtensionManagementUtility::addTcaSelectItemGroup() adds a group to the CType selector, positioned with before:<group> or after:<group>, so several elements of one extension arrive together instead of scattered through the list.
What the element owns before its first field is content-element-shape, and its backend preview is content-element-preview.

Whether it then renders correctly is another layer's answer. A functional test asserts the HTML the template produced; what a reader gets on the page is browser-tests, and browser-tests-outside-core is the site a project's specs run against.

hints.text: What the element owns is decided before its first field, and it is the one decision the rest of it cannot be refactored out of: fields on tt_content for a bounded element; a child table of its own with type=inline for a repeatable ordered collection — slides, tabs, accordion panels — where the parent owns each child's sorting, translation, visibility and deletion; a reference to existing records where reuse is a requirement somebody stated, and the referenced record keeps its own lifecycle and renders wherever else it is referenced; a container of arbitrary tt_content where arbitrary nesting is a requirement somebody stated. The last two are technically possible for a list of slides and are what an element ends up with when the editor workflow was never described: they hand the editor a lifecycle that belongs somewhere else.

title: The Backend Preview of a Content Element
hints: The backend preview of an element is a Fluid template registered in page TSconfig as mod.web_layout.tt_content.preview.<CType>, and the rendering definition is TypoScript: tt_content.<CType> on top of lib.contentElement. Which template that renders is the definition's own templateName rather than anything the CType derives by itself, and sitepackage-templates carries both configurations.

That template replaces the content half of the preview and nothing around it. GridColumnItem::getPreview() renders the header first and dispatches the event the Fluid renderer listens on after it, so the listener's output becomes the content alone. The header is already four parts: the notice where header_layout hides the header, the date field with its label, the record type's label field linked to the edit form — header on tt_content — and subheader. The footer below the content carries starttime, endtime, fe_group, space_before_class, space_after_class and the internal description. So a template that renders {record.header}, {record.subheader} or {record.date} shows them twice, and what it owes the editor is what those parts do not already say.

What it draws instead is the element's own payload, so that two instances of one element are told apart in the page module without opening either: the text columns stripped of their markup, cropped where they repeat; every file relation as a thumbnail through f:image, a hidden file reference drawn as hidden rather than left out; a link field as its label beside the URI f:uri.typolink resolves for it, and marked as broken where it resolves to none; a select as the translated label of the chosen item rather than as the stored value; each child of an inline relation as a line of its own, by the columns that identify the child. None of the core's own previews renders a label naming the element, and the only header any of them draws is a child's.

hints.text: That preview template is handed one variable, record. The columns of the row are no longer variables of their own, so a template that reads {header} renders an empty spot and logs nothing.

Beside record, the preview template is handed every column of the row as a variable of its own — {header}, {bodytext} — and a plugin's FlexForm as {pi_flexform_transformed}. Reading the same values off record is what keeps the template working on the next major.

The core's own worked previews are theme_camino's Resources/Private/Templates/ContentPreviews/, where one template iterates an inline relation with f:for and another renders a file field through f:image.

hints: Whether the preview came out right is not readable from the template either: the page module renders it inside the backend, so what an editor sees is asserted in a browser test rather than in a functional one. browser-tests is that cell.

title: What a Fluid Preview Template Is Handed
appliesTo: what record is as a PHP type

hints.text: {record.header} resolves through the record's container methods: the record is a PSR-11 container, and Fluid asks has() and get() for a path segment before it tries any getter. So every field is {record.<column>}, and {record.uid} and {record.pid} are there as well.

The record is a TYPO3\CMS\Core\Domain\RecordInterface, built by RecordFactory::createResolvedRecordFromDatabaseRow(). The backend preview renderer and the frontend record transformation both call that, so a column carries the same value in a preview template as in a frontend partial.

Only the fields the record type's schema declares are on the record. The enable fields, the timestamps, the sorting and the language and workspace columns are not: they become system properties, reached as {record.systemProperties.disabled} or {record.systemProperties.createdAt}. A path that hits neither raises nothing and resolves to null, so a field that is not there is an empty preview.

A relational field comes back as records rather than as the uid list in the column, and that covers type=select with a relation, group, inline, category and file. A field that relates to many is a lazy collection f:for iterates and f:if counts, each item a record read the same way — {item.title}; one that relates to one is the record itself, or null where the relation is broken. A file field yields the file references f:image takes. Nothing is queried until the template touches the field.

The classes those arrive as are TYPO3\CMS\Core\Collection\LazyRecordCollection and TYPO3\CMS\Core\Resource\Collection\LazyFileReferenceCollection where the field relates to many, and the record interface itself or TYPO3\CMS\Core\Resource\FileReference where it relates to one.
type=select without a relation is a static list and stays values: an array of the selected values, or the single value where the renderType is selectSingle.

Beside the relations, resolving a record turns further columns into objects: type=link into a TYPO3\CMS\Core\LinkHandling\TypolinkParameter, type=datetime into a \DateTimeImmutable, type=flex into a TYPO3\CMS\Core\Domain\FlexFormFieldValues, and type=folder into a TYPO3\CMS\Core\Resource\Folder or a TYPO3\CMS\Core\Resource\Collection\LazyFolderCollection. A type=json column comes back decoded, a nullable link and a folder relating to one are null where nothing is there, and every other column — input, text, number, check — stays what the row stores.
type=country is the other transformed column: a TYPO3\CMS\Core\Country\Country, or an empty string where the stored code matches none.

f:argument declares those types, and what it declares is checked when the template or partial renders: nothing earlier catches a wrong one. The strict processor takes an interface name, so record is declared as TYPO3\CMS\Core\Domain\RecordInterface — array is refused, because a PSR-11 container is not one — and a link column as TypolinkParameter rather than string. Rendering a partial for one section skips the check altogether.

title: Markup Stored in a Field Is Not a Content Model
hints: The core html element renders its bodytext through f:format.raw, so whatever is stored is handed to the visitor as it stands. Nothing about that content is a field: it cannot be queried, translated one part at a time, restyled, or rendered anywhere but where the markup already puts it.

So a page that arrived as one element has been pasted rather than modelled. The unit of a content model is the shape that recurs across pages — a team list, a fee table, a bullet list with links — and each of those is an element with fields of its own, whatever the source stored it as.

The symptom reads as an editing complaint rather than as an architecture one: an editor says the content cannot be maintained, or that everything is one block. What it means is that the modelling step was skipped, and the repair is the elements plus a migration of the stored markup into them.

Which types an editor may create is a separate decision and a site's own: content-element-selector-restriction has the page TSconfig that makes it, and removing an element from the selector leaves every record already stored under it exactly as it is.
